patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Notion and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Notion only if your buying job matches “Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo ann” rather than Trello's shape. Choose Trello only if your buying job matches “Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.” rather than Notion's shape. Workflow advantage: Notion leans work-management; Trello leans project-tracking. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Notion and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Notion is Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo annual; AI on Business.; Trello is Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual..
- Workflow coverage skew: Notion-leaning work-management vs Trello-leaning project-tracking.
- Researched limits: Notion — Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management; Trello — Limited planning depth vs Work OS.

Limitations — Notion: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management; Reporting/dashboards thinner than dedicated PM tools; Trello: Limited planning depth vs Work OS; Premium needed for richer views.

Poor-fit cases: Notion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management · Trello is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Limited planning depth vs Work OS · Avoid Notion if you actually need Trello's motion (Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
